subject: Maths
title: Finding the hypotenuse
subtitle: Pythagoras' Theorem · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can use Pythagoras' theorem to find the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle.

key_vocab.definition: The hypotenuse is the longest side of a right-angled triangle, opposite the right angle. Use c² = a² + b² then square root.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can use Pythagoras' theorem to find the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: hypotenuse -- The hypotenuse is the longest side of a right-angled triangle, opposite the right angle. Use c² = a² + b² then square root.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Square both shorter sides, add them, then square root to find the hypotenuse.
c = √(a² + b²)
Hypotenuse = √(sum of squares of shorter sides)

Key examples:
  ✓ a = 3, b = 4: c = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5  (3-4-5 triple)
  ✓ a = 5, b = 12: c = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13  (5-12-13 triple)
  ✓ a = 6, b = 8: c = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10  (6-8-10 triple)
  ✗ c = a + b = 3 + 4 = 7  (must square, add, then root)
  ✗ c = √(a + b) = √7  (must square a and b first)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – Pythagorean triple
  Find the hypotenuse when a = 6 and b = 8.
  c² = 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100
  c = √100
  c = 10
  c = 10
  (6, 8, 10 is a Pythagorean triple (multiple of 3, 4, 5).)

Example 2 – non-integer answer
  Find the hypotenuse when a = 5 and b = 7.
  c² = 5² + 7² = 25 + 49 = 74
  c = √74
  c = 8.60 (2 d.p.)
  c = 8.60
  (Leave as √74 for exact form, or round for decimal.)

sections.title: Integer answers (triples)
sections.content:
Find the hypotenuse.

(a) a = 3, b = 4
(b) a = 5, b = 12
(c) a = 8, b = 15
(d) a = 9, b = 40

sections.title: Decimal answers
sections.content:
Find c to 1 d.p.

(a) a = 4, b = 6
(b) a = 3, b = 7
(c) a = 5, b = 9
(d) a = 2, b = 8

sections.title: Word problems
sections.content:
Find the hypotenuse in each situation.

(a) Walk 6 km East then 8 km North. Direct distance?
(b) Gate 3 m wide, 4 m tall. Diagonal brace length?
(c) TV screen 48 cm wide, 36 cm tall. Diagonal?
(d) Triangle: base 7 cm, height 24 cm. Hypotenuse?

sections.title: Larger numbers
sections.content:
Find the hypotenuse. Give exact or rounded answer.

(a) a = 20, b = 21
(b) a = 11, b = 60
(c) a = 14, b = 48
(d) a = 10, b = 10

sections.title: Mixed problems
sections.content:
Find the missing hypotenuse.

(a) Right triangle: legs 9 and 12
(b) Right triangle: legs 7 and 7
(c) Rectangular garden 15 m by 20 m, diagonal path?
(d) Right triangle: legs 1.5 and 2
(e) Right triangle: legs 11 and 13

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ c² = a² + b² then c = √(a² + b²)
✗ The hypotenuse equals a + b
✓ The hypotenuse is always the longest side
✗ c = √(a + b)
✓ 3, 4, 5 and 5, 12, 13 are Pythagorean triples
